text:
Maya: Heads-up — US-WEST spot eviction rate jumped to ~12% this week, variance ~3x vs baseline. Thinking we need a smoothing buffer + different allocation mix. Anyone have quick econ thoughts on mixing around 40/60 on-demand/spot vs leaning all-in on spot?

Raj: Can you paste the raw numbers? what's the median run length and cost/hr you're using?

Maya: quick raw: eviction=12%, baseline=4%, on-demand $3.20/hr, spot mean $0.98/hr, spot sd ~$0.40/hr. Rough relocation penalty ~1.5x for lost throughput during failover. So naive effective spot cost = 0.98 + 0.12*(1.5*3.20) approx.

Linda: @Maya good framing. FinOps prefers modeling expected unit cost and a reserve for variance. Suggest we compute E[cost] and also a 95th pctile for budgeting. Example formula: 
```
E_cost = p_on * C_on + p_spot * C_spot + eviction_rate * relocation_penalty
where p_on + p_spot = 1
relocation_penalty ≈ probability_eviction * cost_of_recovery
```

Kevin: Two quick notes — regional correlation matters (we saw correlated interruptions last month) so mixing across regions reduces tail risk. Also for latency-sensitive routes keep a higher on-demand floor.

Raj: I ran a quick Monte Carlo (1k sims): mix 60/40 (on/spot) gives mean cost ~22% lower than pure on-demand, but stddev of unit cost is ~40% lower than pure spot. I can upload CSV.

Maya: Proposal draft: default pool mix 60/40 for user-facing SLOs, 80/20 for batch/low-priority. Chargeback: allocate forecasted spot savings to product teams monthly, but retain 20% of realized savings in infra for a smoothing reserve. Thoughts? :chart_with_upwards_trend: 

Linda: I like that. For chargeback we'll need both forecast vs realized and a variance line item so finance can reconcile each quarter. Also recommend a small reserve fund (1-2% of infra budget) to cover eviction spikes.

ops-bot: [automated] US-WEST spot pool eviction trend: 4w MA 7.8% -> 9.6% -> 11.3% -> 12.0% (current).

Maya: OK I'll draft a short RFC with the numbers + sample chargeback calc. @Kevin can you run regional correlation analysis and attach the Monte Carlo gist? I'll loop in finance for the reserve account.

Kevin: on it, will upload the gist in the RFC thread later today.

Linda: thanks — ping me on the RFC, we'll add the forecast reconciliation table so chargeback is transparent.
